If the yellow light never flashes at all on the wixel then there is a problem there. Check wiring but also try reloading the .wxl firmware file. Sometimes they get corrupted, sometimes wixels completely die.

wefink,
You initially said that the wixel yellow LED was permanently flashing, but
the HM-1x green LED was off.  This should not happen.  It would indicate to
me that either the HM-1x is not being powered by the wixel, or the HM-1x is
faulty.

In order to help I need you to be very clear on the state of the LEDs on
both modules.

If BOTH the wixel yellow LED is flashing and the HM-1x LED is flashing,
that is good and means that the HM-1x module is powered and the Bluetooth
connection has not been established with xDrip/xDrip+.

However, this should NOT stay this way unless the G4 transmitter is out of
range of the bridge.

If the G4 IS in range of the bridge, then the wixel yellow LED should only
flash for around 2 minutes before going off.  The HM-1x LED should do the
same.

This means that the wixel has seen a packet of data from the G4, hasn't
been able to see the Bluetooth connection to xDrip/xDrip+ is up, and has
gone to sleep.  Approximately 3 minutes later it will wake up and start
flashing the Yellow LED again, and hopefully the green LED on the HM-1x is
also flashing.  This shows that the HM-1x is powered up and ready to
connect.

If the LED on the HM-1x is NOT flashing at all while the wixel yellow LED
is flashing, then there is a problem.  Either the connection of the Status
line from the HM-1x to the wixel is broken, or the VSS line between the
HM-1x and the wixel is broken, or the HM-1x is broken.

I have never lost a Wixel yet, but there were a batch with bad crystals in
them that would not always reliably capture a packet from the G4.  I have
had HM-1x modules go bad in various ways.

Do you have a multi-meter to measure the voltages on the HM-1x pins?

When the wixel is awake, there should be approximately 3.3V (higher is OK)
between VCC and GND pins on the HM-1x.  If there is not, there is a problem
in the wiring/soldering to the HM-1x on the VCC and/or GND lines.

Also, there should be a pulse of 3.3V between the GND and the P1_2 pins on
the wixel

The Red LED will blink (once very 1/2 second) IF the wixel has communicated
with xDrip/xDrip+ and gotten a G4 Transmitter ID from there.  It will blink
until it has captured a packet from the G4 transmitter, when it will go off.

The Yellow LED will blink until the HM-1x LED has gone solid ON for 1/2
second, then it will stay on while the wixel is awake and the HM-1x LED
stays solid, waiting for a packet from the configured G4 Transmitter.

If the LED on the HM-1x Bluetooth board is blinking, this is indicating
that it does NOT have a connection with xDrip/xDrip+.  The wixel Yellow LED
will therefore be blinking also.

There should be NO variation from the above at any time.  If there is any
variation from these states, please let us know.  It is likely that you
have a soldering or wiring issue between the two modules, or one or the
other module is faulty.  Money is on the HM-1x if it is.

You need to make sure the HM-1x is NOT paired to your phone's Bluetooth
settings, and IS paired in xDrip/xDrip+.  In fact, there should be no way
that you can pair it to your phone, unless it is in the incorrect operating
mode, as the phones do not usually scan BTLE/BT4.0 Low Energy mode.
However, xDrip/xDrip+ can scan for BTLE/Low Energy mode devices.

Please do the following.
Note, the instructions below are based on xDrip, as I do not use xDrip+
yet.  If someone with experience with xDrip+ can please correct any of my
instructions if there is an issue, I would appreciate it.

1) Go into xDrip/xDrip+ System Status and "Forget Device".
2) Go into the your phone's Bluetooth settings and make certain that there
is no xBridgeXXYY device

Hi Wefink,
Link to xBridge2.wxl is
https://github.com/jstevensog/wixel-sdk/blob/master/apps/xBridge2/xBridge2.wxl
.
What you are describing about the wixel Red LED blinking 4 times, then
waiting 10 seconds, then another 4 times, and ongoing, is normal.
This is saying that the wixel has been flashed with a new xBridge2 program,
and it has NOT yet received it's transmitter ID from xDrip.

The fact that the HM-1x module is still flashing it's LED says that does
not have a connection with xDrip.  And of course, if you don't have this
connection, the xBridge2 program cannot get the G4 transmitter ID from
xDrip.  So, the wixel Red LED will continue to flash 4 times every 10
seconds.

Either you do not have the xBridgeXXYY device paired in xDrip/xDrip+, or
there is something wrong with the HM-1x.  All indications are that the
wixel is fine at this point.  By XXYY, I mean 4 letters/numbers appended
after "xBridge".  This uniquely identifies your xBridge.  For example, mine
is "xBridge63f7".

Did you go through the steps I outlined yesterday?
Did you make sure to Forget Device in the System Status page of
xDrip/xDrip+?
Did you then scan for your xBridgeXXYY device?  Did you find it, and select
it?

If you did those things and could not find the xBridgeXXYY device to
connect to, then the issue is definitely with the HM-1x module.  Replace it
and you should be fine.

You can also use an app on your phone called "BLE Scanner" to search.  It
will only show BLE devices that are NOT connected to something.  It will
not show an xBridge that has been connected to xDrip.  Once you find it,
you can "connect" to it, and the HM-1x LED will go solid, and the Yellow
LED on the wixel will go solid 0.5 second later.

Don't give up, you will get to the bottom of it.
Cheers

Hi Wefink,
Sorry for the long delay in getting back to you.

Is the Wixel Red LED blinking regularly or doing some flashes, then off,
then flashes, then off......?

Where you said, Red on wixel not blinking anymore, and Green on BT is off,
then later blinking again, this says to me that the wixel caught a Dexcom
packet, but the the connection with xDrip could not be made, so the wixel
went to sleep about 2 minutes after capturing the packet.  So, the main
issue here is that the BT is NOT connecting to the phone.

To remove the xBridge from xDrip, you go into System Status and press the
Forget Device button.  I am not sure if this is the same with xDrip+ or
not, so check with the xDrip+ guys if you are using that.  I am yet to move
to it.

Once you have removed the xBridge from xDrip(+), you can scan for the
xBridge (IF IT IS AWAKE) in xDrip(+) and select it.

It should then be connected in the System Status page, unless it has
captured a packet and gone back to sleep.

To save battery, xBridge by default will only try to send a packet to xDrip
for 2 minutes, then go to sleep, turning off the BT when it does so.  You
can change this behaviour using a command to xBridge if you connect the
wixel to a computer USB port and run a terminal program like PuTTY.  The
xBridge2.pdf file has all that information in it.

Again, sorry for the long delay in responding.  My email inbox is getting
out of hand, and I have been extremely busy.
Cheers
